paragraphs: Here's what I take from Ephesus, friend. Jesus is not a name you borrow. The sons of Sceva said, "I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims," and the spirit answered, "Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?" (Acts 19:13, 15). They had the words, but they didn't have Him, and that is the difference between knowing about Jesus and knowing Him.

Notice what the Ephesians did once they saw it. Many who had believed came forward, "confessing and disclosing their deeds," and those who had practiced magic arts burned their books in front of everyone (Acts 19:18-19). Fifty thousand drachmas of books, gone, and nobody was asking for a refund. When Jesus is held in high honor, I think the things that competed with Him start to look like day-old crumbs (Acts 19:17).

So here's my question for you, baker. Is Jesus someone you know, or someone you quote? Paul went back to the start with those twelve men, because the start matters, and he kept talking to everyone who would listen, so that "the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail" (Acts 19:20). Keep your oven ready, friend, and let Him be the one you know. The story isn't over, either.
